entities.summary: Amanieu d'Albret was a French Roman Catholic cardinal born in 1480 to the noble Albret family in the region of Gascony, which he represented in the French Parliament. He served as Bishop of Limoges from 1505 until his death in 1520. During his tenure, he played a crucial role in the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation, advocating for a more conservative approach to theology and liturgy. His efforts contributed to the eventual Council of Trent, a major gathering of Catholic clergy that aimed to reform the Church and counter the influence of Protestantism. This council, held from 1545 to 1563, would go on to shape the Church's doctrine and practices for centuries to come. As a key figure in the Church's response to the Reformation, d'Albret's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of Catholicism in Europe and beyond. In the annals of history, his commitment to the Church's traditional teachings and his role in shaping the Council of Trent stand as a testament to his enduring significance. The Catholic Church's response to the Reformation, in which d'Albret played a pivotal role, had far-reaching consequences, including the establishment of the Jesuits and the Catholic Counter-Reformation.
